scope_description: Read-only current-snapshot parity review at f44d6010d923f3e90bba7e1e16bb6a0d4f86875d. Compare bee's Codex and Claude Code harness paths for equivalent workflow information and steps: onboarding and injected instructions, lifecycle hooks, routing and gate state, dispatch and role/model selection, worker brief construction, spawn/tending/wait behavior, write and secret guards, result and evidence return, and close/recovery behavior. This is a behavior audit, not a release diff. Exclude model quality, provider availability, and all uncommitted local state.
head: f44d6010d923f3e90bba7e1e16bb6a0d4f86875d

reviewers.reason: prepared Codex task_name violates live API charset

reviewer_manifest.local_inspection: source trace plus live dispatch, live tool validation, doctor, and targeted Rust tests

dismissed.reason: bee-* SKILL.md path comparison returned no differences; Claude has three unrelated product skills

dismissed.suspicion: Codex lacks the core safety hooks
dismissed.reason: manifest contains session-init, prompt-context, write-guard, model-guard, state-sync, tools-logger, chain-nudge, session-close, and subagent audit
working config carries matching role names for Claude and Codex; model and transport values differ by provider

findings.title: Codex native dispatch emits an invalid task_name
findings.scenario: A Codex gather, reviewer, advisor, or titled cell uses a subject such as reviewer: Compare ... as task_name. The current spawn_agent API rejects the call because task_name accepts only lowercase letters, digits, and underscores. No worker starts.
findings.evidence: Live prepare emitted task_name with colon, spaces, and uppercase text. The exact spawn_agent call was rejected: agent_name must use only lowercase letters, digits, and underscores. Source lines 1900-1903 copy subject directly. Test drivers/tests.rs:1087-1104 pins the invalid c-1: title form and passes.
findings.recommendation: Create a stable slug for task_name. Put the full subject and assignment in message. Add a live-schema conformance test.

findings.title: Non-cell dispatch drops the requested assignment from worker input
findings.scenario: The orchestrator passes --purpose with the concrete review or gather task. Bee keeps it only in task_name or description. The message, prompt, or stdin contains only the generic role template. A worker starts without the requested scope or question.
findings.evidence: Live Codex and Claude prepare outputs both had generic review or gather bodies. CLI branches write pane_prompt at lines 1748-1755 and 1775-1782; the herding branch repeats this at 1796-1822. The purpose becomes subject only at lines 1676-1684.
findings.recommendation: Append the full purpose to prompt_body or pane_prompt for every non-cell transport. Keep task_name and description as short labels only.

findings.title: Concurrent herding runs can reuse one millisecond job id
findings.scenario: Parallel dispatch starts two or more herding jobs in one millisecond. Each derives the same job-<timestamp_millis> id and writes the same mailbox. One run can remove or overwrite state used by another.
findings.evidence: Three live parallel runs all produced job-1789125757006. One failed because its job.json path vanished while another used the same mailbox. Source line 364 uses only timestamp_millis; no uniqueness suffix or exclusive retry exists.
findings.recommendation: Use a collision-resistant id or atomically reserve the mailbox and retry on AlreadyExists. Add a concurrent start test.

findings.title: The installed Bee binary is one release behind the source
findings.scenario: Both runtimes call .bee/bin/bee from their hook manifests. That binary reports release 2.34.0 while the source and plugin report 2.35.0, so new source behavior is not active in hooks.
findings.evidence: bee doctor --runtime codex and --runtime claude both returned overall_status blocked. Their binary_freshness row reports installed 2.34.0 versus source 2.35.0. Plugin line 3 declares 2.35.0.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild and install the current binary, then rerun both doctor checks.

findings.title: Codex does not provide the same lifecycle activity and trust evidence
findings.scenario: A Codex session works through tool failures, permission waits, notifications, or session end. Bee receives no activity checkpoint for these events. Supervisors can see no_signal where Claude records working, waiting, or exited. Hook discovery and trust also remain unknown without attestation.
findings.evidence: The Codex manifest has 8 events; Claude has 11. Claude-only events are Notification, PermissionRequest, PostToolUseFailure, and SessionEnd; Claude also emits activity on prompt/tool/stop events. The knowledge rule at line 73 names this as an allowed difference. doctor reports four Codex trust rows unknown and doctor::tests::codex_stops_at_degraded_where_claude_reaches_ready passes.
findings.recommendation: Treat this as a declared capability gap. Add Codex events when the host exposes them, and require a valid attestation before claiming runtime readiness.

findings.title: The declared full test command is red on the current snapshot
findings.scenario: A release or parity claim uses the repository's declared cargo test command. The bee binary test target reports 64 failures, and the concurrency integration target reports 2 failures. Later hook tests then run longer than 150 seconds and the audit stops them after red is already established.
findings.evidence: Fresh command: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/bee-harness-parity-target cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml. Output: 3405 passed, 64 failed, 20 ignored in bee unit tests; concurrency: 17 passed, 2 failed. Exit was 130 after interrupting two integration tests that stayed active beyond 150 seconds.
findings.recommendation: Make the declared suite green in the same Codex session environment. Separate environment-sensitive failures from product failures, then rerun the exact command.

decision.summary: Current Codex harness is not fully equivalent to Claude Code. Five P1 findings block a parity claim; one P2 is a documented host-capability gap. Independent reviewer dispatch itself was blocked by parity-1. The lead source-traced and live-reproduced the findings; the declared full suite is red.
